speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you describe exactly what happens during these episodes, specifically how long they last and if you regain consciousness immediately afterward? I also need to know if there is any warning sign or aura you feel before the unresponsiveness begins.

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the hand gestures involve rhythmic movements like picking at clothes or rubbing his face, and has he experienced any loss of bowel or bladder control during these episodes? I also need to know if these events tend to occur when he is falling asleep, waking up, or during daytime activities.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: EEG. The presence of an olfactory/gustatory aura (muddy taste), followed by automatisms and post-ictal confusion, strongly suggests focal seizures, likely originating from the temporal or insular lobe. I need to confirm epileptiform activity to proceed.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG confirms right temporal lobe epilepsy. To rule out a structural cause for these seizures, I need to visualize the brain anatomy. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI is normal, these are likely idiopathic focal seizures. Have you tried any anti-seizure medications yet, and if so, have they reduced the frequency or severity of these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRI and confirmed right temporal lobe EEG findings, this presents as focal epilepsy without a structural cause. Since no medication has been tried yet, we will initiate treatment with an appropriate anti-seizure drug like levetiracetam. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
